lens: Motion director + production lead. Ten criteria, 1-10 each: (1) MOTION-NATIVE: the movement is the idea, not a sweep added to a still; (2) CALM/PREMIUM pace against the owner's tuning (35 s box turn, 10 s flower, no jitter, no flashes, no lyrics); (3) STORYBOARD craft: beats, holds (words >= 1.2 s), first-second hook, variety across the run; (4) LOOP LOGIC: reels and carousel loops seamless, slide-1 frame 0 = cover; (5) END CARDS and lockup: consistent, readable, held >= 2.5 s; (6) SOUND direction: instrumental only, timed SFX, a sonic signature; (7) COVERS AND GRID at 391x521: tiles read, the piece reads, the 12 covers compose; (8) FEASIBILITY on our pipeline (HTML/CSS/SVG seeked by tools/reel.cjs, BiRefNet cut-outs, <= 25 AI layer plates; flags real footage, character animation, complex 3D, upsampling); (9) FINISH CEILING vs AMATEUR RISK at a 10/10 bar (drawing quality an agent can reach, AI-plate tells, collage mismatch); (10) PRODUCTION PLAN: shared kit, build order, fallbacks, render load. Checked against the real kit: tools/reel.cjs is fixed at 1080x1920 (carousel loops need a 1080x1440 twin; all four note it); the motion demos (_strip, _bstrip) prove shutter, tube light, glint, drawer and pop-up layers; the cut-outs are small (brushed-gold-huggies 370 px, woven hoops 589, fine tennis 777, most 600-1000 px on the long side), so any push-in or loupe past about 1.2x on a cut-out goes soft; work/v3box/proto/p2-full.png is the only V3 render to exist and it looks flat and clip-art (karwa, box faces, dark stage floor).

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-free.json · NAIRA NIWAS (one building, one window a post)
scores.criteria: 1 motion-native 9: every reel opens on the whole building at exactly 1/3 scale, which is the profile grid, finds this week's window, opens it, lights it and pulls back to a building with one more window lit; the series accumulates on screen and on the profile, so the motion is the idea at post level AND at season level (P12's wedding lights unfurling down all twelve bays is the payoff). 2 calm 8: the kandil turns once per 10.0 s (the owner's flower number), the drawer uses the site's 1.1 s / 1.0 s, camera moves 1.8-2.0 s for a 3x zoom (far calmer than GALLI's 8x in 2.2 s), nothing from scale 0, no bounce; minus for P8's chit flutter (+-3 deg every 1.25 s, eight cycles) and P9's notice flutter (1.5 s), which read as fidget, and two 120 ms tube blinks. 3 storyboard 8: exact, camera maths given (window.atTime formula), headline holds >= 2 s, P7's three type beats over a closed curtain are real comic timing; minus because six reels share a ~7 s wrapper (establish, find, pull-back, card) and several carousel slide-1 loops are only ambient (P2 S1 a light band over the bangle wall, P5 S1 a shadow drift, P11 S1 wisps): exactly the 'sweep on a still' it criticises in A. 4 loop 8: reels dissolve from end card to frame 0 (a soft seam, honest), carousel frame 0 = cover, P9's kandil phase-locked to 9 s; P11 S2 moonrise loops by cross-fade (a cheat). 5 end card 9: brass plate with the real wordmark whose flower turns on the I's stem at 36 deg/s, the site's own behaviour; name, bracket, price, URL; holds 2.9 s on P1 but only 1.9-2.1 s on P4, P7, P10. 6 sound 8: one building-ambience signature on every establishing shot, 2-4 timed foley hits per reel, music ducks under foley; carousels silent; no lyrics. 7 grid 9: the strongest grid of the four: twelve covers assemble into one Deco building standing on the LAC pavement, pilasters and string courses run across every gutter, a blush kandil at the same spot top-left of every tile, pieces at true scale inside windows (P1 bracelet 188 px in the grid); risk: twelve tiles of blush plaster can read samey, and the terrace end of the gradient (#DEA99D) edges toward the tan the owner dislikes. 8 feasibility 7: one C-WORLD file (3258x5787) with 12 bay components x 3 states; all 2D except shutters/doors on rotateY and an optional three.js box render via SwiftShader (fallback SVG); 18 AI plates, all props shot at one stated angle (35 deg above) so they sit together; it caught the 370 px huggie cut-out (CUT-V3-03) and the marquise plinth recut; front-loaded: all 12 bays' closed states must exist for P1's first frame. 9 finish 7: the facade is geometry agents draw well; interiors are photographs (AI props + real cut-outs) at true relative scale, so the doll's-house split is coherent rather than a clash; the 2D 'torsion' of the kandil (facet widths swapping) must be checked frame by frame or it will read as breathing, not turning; P12's 26 strands over the whole building is the hardest frame. 10 plan 8: build C-WORLD and C-KANDIL first, prove P1 end to end, residents recur, fallbacks for every Devanagari string and every AI plate. AMATEUR RISK BY POST: P1 low · P2 low-med · P3 med (box renders, four drawer loops) · P4 low · P5 med (newsprint and vati must come out blank and true) · P6 low · P7 low-med · P8 med (fine chains on green, teak table) · P9 low-med · P10 med (AI dupattas) · P11 low-med · P12 med-high (whole-building light curtain, tower, emerald set on AI silk). No real footage, no character animation; no complex 3D required.
best_posts: P12 EVEN THE BUILDING DRESSED UP: wedding lights unfurl down all twelve bays, the tower's name lights, then the emerald-green set; the pull-back frame IS the finished profile. The single best motion idea in the competition.
P1 BACK IN 5 MINUTES: shutter rolls up on a tent card that is the headline; owns the 76-day silence; ends on a building with one window lit.

P6 NO OIL. NO WICK.: three panatis light left to right while the glint runs along the Rivière Eternal in step, then burn out right to left and the bracelet stays lit: light is the joke and the motion.
P7 KAHI NAKO: three type beats over a glowing voile, the curtain draws, the drawer slides out at the site's 1.1 s; the best comic timing of the four proposals.
weakest_posts: P2 NO SOAP REQUIRED: slide-1 loop is only a light band crossing the bangle wall plus a glint (decoration, not idea), and the soap joke duplicates GALLI P2.
P5 TAMARIND AND LEMON: slide-1 motion is a drifting fanlight shadow and dust motes; the real action (the polish wipe) is buried on slide 2.
P11 THE MOON IS BACK: wisps and a breathing halo on the cover; slide 2's moonrise loops by cross-fade; the quietest idea in the run.
P8 TWO NECKLACES: the chit's 1.25 s flutter is fidget; the joke lives in the copy, not the motion.
must_fix: Hold every reel end card >= 2.5 s (P4 2.1 s, P7 2.1 s, P10 1.9 s today).
Slow or remove fidget loops: P8 chit (1.25 s, +-3 deg) to one slow +-1.5 deg sway on 3.2 s or still; P9 notice to 3.2 s; keep the two 120 ms tube blinks only on P1.

Give every carousel slide 1 a native action, not a sweep: P2 (the bangle-wala's hand slides a glass stack aside / the cuff opens on its gap), P5 (move the polish wipe onto slide 1), P11 (let the moon clear the parapet on slide 1).

Prove the kandil torsion in a 10 s test render before anything else: if the facet-width swap reads as pulsing, build it as a CSS 3D octahedron (two pyramids, rotateY) or replace torsion with sway only.

Render all 12 covers as a 3x4 composite above LAC / flower / BONE at 391x521 before week 1: check the blush monotony and that #DEA99D (terrace) does not read tan; deepen toward rose, not brown, if it does.
Decide the box early: test the three.js render under SwiftShader on day 1, else commit to the SVG box; never mix the two looks.
Front-load C-WORLD: P1's establishing frame shows all twelve bays closed, so every facade, shutter, curtain and gate state must be drawn and checked at 1/3 scale before 27 Oct.
P3's WhatsApp 'three options with photographs' is the same staffed-service promise it faults in A: owner sign-off or cut.
graftable: The establishing shot = the profile grid at 1/3 scale (lit windows accumulate week by week): the strongest serial motion device in the competition.
End-card wordmark whose flower turns on the I's stem at 36 deg/s from naira-wordmark-geometry.json: the site's own motion, usable by any option.
One stated camera angle (35 deg above) and a per-post set scale in px/mm for every prop and cut-out: the cleanest anti-collage-clash rule written.
The kandil as a 10 s turning emblem, true for every date 27 Oct to 22 Nov (Kartik).
Lamps lighting in step with a glint travelling along a line of stones (P6), reusable for any tennis/rivière piece.

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-illustrated-films.json · DRAWN FROM LIFE (twelve small films)
scores.criteria: 1 motion-native 9: the thesis cannot exist as a still: a drawn everyday shape match-dissolves into the photographed piece in its exact footprint (plait to braid, aarti trail to the ruby ellipse, rangoli border to Prism, mehendi dots-to-drop to Mint Pear), then the drawing un-draws and 'the piece stays'. The best-written motion grammar of the four. 2 calm 8: one nib at 520 px/s, at most one camera move per film (<= 1.06 except P1's slow 4 s push to 2.4), no cuts, nothing faster than 600 ms in type; minus for P5's rub (+-6 deg three times in 600 ms = 5 Hz scrub, the one jitter in the run) and P4's 3-frame match spark. 3 storyboard 8: a fixed four-beat grammar (draw, rhyme, line, piece stays) with per-film rhymes that are genuinely witty; minus for frame 0 being blank paper plus a horizon line (the weakest first second of the four for the Reels tab), and eight films sharing the same un-draw/label tail. 4 loop 8: every film fades back to the empty page = frame 0; flipbook slide 1 is cover-first; fade-to-blank is a soft but honest seam. 5 end card 9: the gallery label with the piece alone on the page and 'the moment goes. the piece stays.' is the most elegant end card proposed; label holds ~2.9 s visible. 6 sound 9: nib scratch under every drawing and one 'ting' when the piece lands: a true sonic logo; instrumental only, per-film instruments, pauses timed to gags (P2 cloud B, P8 skipped beat). 7 grid 9 -> 8: day/night paper checkerboard climbing out of LAC/flower/BONE, one horizon line per row, signed margins, headlines 84-120 px; pieces 85-230 px in the grid; reads as a sketchbook wall. 8 feasibility 6: no 3D, no WebGL, all 2D, render-safe resolutions; BUT the core effect, 'a steel nib drawing an AI line plate', depends on hand-authored centre-line mask strokes (36 px) in drawing order for 12 figure plates: slow, error-prone, and without them it reads as a wipe, not a pen; plus CSS d morph (P7), feTurbulence wet edges via atTime, ~30 clips. 9 finish 5: the highest ceiling (Hermes-film territory) and the highest amateur risk: 12 AI anatomy plates (hands, ears, napes, palms, a waist) must look like one hand and not 'generated'; agent SVG objects must match through an #ink filter; rigid moves of line-art hands read as paper puppetry; photographed pieces wrapped round drawn limbs (P2 bangle on a raised forearm, P11 an open flat-lay bracelet 'shaped' to a wrist, P9 four necklaces masked to front arcs) will look pasted. 10 plan 7: P1 as the template reviewed with the owner first, one retry per plate, fallbacks to agent single-line gestures. AMATEUR RISK BY POST: P1 high (two head/hand plates, draw-on, plate cross-dissolve during push) · P2 high (silhouette + bangle round a raised arm) · P3 low-med (geometric tiffin, agent-strong) · P4 med (hand plate, rigid aarti orbit) · P5 med-high (rub jitter, hand plate) · P6 low (rangoli is pure geometry: the safest, most beautiful post) · P7 med (hands + ribbon morph) · P8 low-med (card, lamp) · P9 high (neck plate, four necklines, masked necklaces) · P10 high (two palms, ear, helper's fingers) · P11 high (waist and pleats plate, pins-to-bracelet round a wrist) · P12 high (side-back head, hand at lobe, drawn jhumka). No real footage; no true character animation, but eight posts depend on drawn anatomy.
best_posts: P6 A RANGOLI LASTS ONE NIGHT: the flipbook IS the process (dots, lines, colour, then a broom sweeps all of it away and leaves the Prism Riviere): the most native carousel in the competition, and the safest to build.
P1 MUMMY'S PLAIT: the plait's over-under dissolves into the Woven Gold Hoop's braid at the lobe; teaches the season's grammar in 18 s.
P4 RED, LIKE THE TILAK: the aarti lamp's gold trail closes into an ellipse that becomes the Ruby bracelet in the thali; forwardable, eight days early.
P12 THE HEAVY ONES COME OFF AT 2 A.M.: the jhumka goes to the locker box, the huggie stays and glints; the thesis as a scene.
weakest_posts: P5 EVERYTHING GETS POLISHED: 5 Hz rubbing is the jitter the owner sends back; the rhyme (heap outline to chain) is the weakest of the twelve.
P11 NOBODY SEES THE SAFETY PINS: pins drift to a drawn wrist and 'become' a flat-lay open bracelet masked as an arc: the composite will look pasted.
P2 THE MOON IS LATE: a photographed bangle split into back and front arcs round a drawn raised forearm at a different perspective: high composite risk on the Karwa Chauth slot.
P9 GALA KAISA CHAHIYE?: neck plate + four necklines + four masked necklaces: the heaviest anatomy-dependent build.
must_fix: Build P1 as a 10 s proof first: one AI line plate revealed by authored centre-line masks, one agent SVG object through #ink, one match-dissolve; if it does not read as a pen at 100%, simplify every figure to agent single-line gestures before committing.
Generate the outline for every rhyme from the cut-out's own alpha (potrace) so the drawn shape and the photograph overlap exactly.
P5: replace the 600 ms triple rub with one slow circle per vessel (1.2 s) or a single wipe.

Never wrap a flat-lay photograph round a drawn limb: P2 lay the bangle on the parapet beside the sieve, P11 let the bracelet land on the pleats, P9 keep each necklace as its own photographed curve, not a masked arc.
Give frame 0 a hook: start with the folio and the first stroke already moving (or the headline at 0.0 s) instead of blank paper.
Lock one style block for all 12 anatomy plates and reject any plate with fused fingers or 'generated' smoothness; the budget leaves only ~7 retries.
graftable: The match-dissolve rhyme (drawn outline traced from the cut-out alpha retracts while the photograph develops in its footprint) as the piece's entrance in any option.
The 14 px paper halo (no drawn line touches the piece) and 'shown larger.' as honesty rules that are also a look.
Process flipbooks whose swipes are stages (P6 rangoli) as the model for carousels that move for a reason.
Nib + ting as a sonic logo; 'the moment goes. the piece stays.' as a sign-off.
P12's 2 a.m. jhumka idea and P10's mehendi-drying idea as windows or scenes in another world.

scores.proposal: v3-proposal-galli.json · NAIRA GALLI (twelve shopfronts on one lane)
scores.criteria: 1 motion-native 8: the rolling shutter is a real, universal reveal with its own sound, and each shop has a diegetic action (money-order form writing itself and the stamp, ladis switching on in a wave synced to the bracelet glint, the eye chart lighting row by row to spell NAIRA GALLI, the press clack, the studio flash); but seven carousel covers move only by ambient sway, shimmer and glint. 2 calm 7: walking-pace rules, E-curves defined, periods that divide loops; minus for P1's pull-back from 2.8x to 0.333x (8.4x) in 2.2 s on ease-in-out (a whoosh), P10's 21 metal sorts dropping at 0.1 s staggers (busy clicking), P4's 0.15 s stamp and the tube's double blink. 3 storyboard 7: rich and exact, diegetic sound cues, but P1's colour beat holds labels 0.6 s (under the 1.2 s word rule) and the reels hold their price card for only 0.2-1.3 s before the loop rolls the shutter up again. 4 loop 9: the best loop logic of the four: every reel starts and ends on the same painted night shutter, so shutter down = end card = frame 0, and every ambient period divides the loop length. 5 end card 7: C-END painted shutter is diegetic and consistent (wordmark, name, material, price, URL, plate), undermined by the sub-second holds. 6 sound 8: rattle up/down as a signature, timed ticks, stamp thump, press clack, instrumental santoor/sitar; metal rattle must be mixed soft. 7 grid 8: each row is one continuous 3,240 px street (shared sky, kerb, ladi) in four hours of light, LAC-red road into the live row, shop names read at 36%; but pieces are small on several covers (P3 hoop ~94 px, P8 Prism ~90 px behind jar glass, P11 studs) and every tile is the same elevation (board, pati, window, plate). 8 feasibility 7: Bombay Deco elevations are the kind of geometry agents draw well and the kit's FANCY STORE demo already proves shutter + tube + glint; 16 AI plates; but P7's loupe magnifies a 777 px cut-out to ~5x (soft), P1 scales AI textures 2.8x, and AI photo props (steel vessels, platen press, flower baskets, sugarcane, box camera) sit inside flat SVG shops. 9 finish 7: Wes-Anderson flatness is forgiving; clip-art risk in dense interiors (spectacle racks, jars, pigeonholes, bangle poles) and in photo-prop-in-flat-world collage. 10 plan 8: components first (facade, board, pati, shutter, plate, end card), P1-P3 against the live row, fallback order, stock guards. AMATEUR RISK BY POST: P1 low-med · P2 low · P3 low · P4 med (stroke-written form, pillar box) · P5 med-high (AI steel cliff in a flat shop) · P6 low · P7 med (loupe softness, racks) · P8 med (jars, fan; piece hidden) · P9 med (new chain cut-out, lockers) · P10 med-high (AI press photo, 21 sorts) · P11 high (AI baskets, sugarcane, banana leaf, busiest tile) · P12 med (AI painted backdrop, camera, umbrellas). No real footage, no character animation, no 3D beyond the shutter.
best_posts: P4 POST OFFICE · BUY SOMETHING NICE.: the money order fills itself in, the NASHIK ROAD stamp lands, the form goes into the pillar box and the bangle priced exactly Rs 999 appears: a complete diegetic story, forwardable.
P7 OPTICIANS · READ THE LAST LINE.: the chart lights row by row spelling NAIRA GALLI, the camera drops from the last line of dots to the line of stones: the craft argument as an eye test.
P6 ELECTRICALS · NO PLUG. NO FUSE.: ladis switch on in a wave and the glint runs along the Riviere Eternal in step.
P1 BACK AFTER LUNCH.: plate unveiled, shutter wave up the row, the key art (once the pull-back is slowed).
weakest_posts: P11 PHOOLWALA: the densest AI collage (baskets mirrored to five, sugarcane V, toran, petals) around a small stud pair; highest amateur risk.
P8 GENERAL STORES: the Prism sits behind tinted jar glass at ~90 px in the grid; the motion is lids and a fan.
P10 WEDDING CARDS: 21 sorts dropping is busy, the AI platen press is a photo in a flat world, and the cuff has no rhyme with 'compliments'.
P12 PHOTO STUDIO: three pieces on velvet steps under an AI painted backdrop and umbrellas: crowded for the top-left tile.
must_fix: Hold every end card >= 2.5 s before the loop: today P4, P6, P7 hold 0.2 s and P10 0.6 s after the shutter lands, so the price is never readable.
P1: slow the pull-back (>= 3.5 s or start at 1.6x, not 2.8x) and hold each colour label >= 1.2 s.
P7: recut the Fine Tennis Bracelet from the full-resolution listing photo or cap the loupe at 1.5x; P11 slide 3 studs are upscaled from 644 px.
P10: set fewer sorts (one word) at >= 0.25 s each, or show the stick already set.
Enlarge the piece on P3, P8 and P11 covers so it reads at 391x521; take P8's bracelet out of the jar for the cover.
Test one AI steel/press/basket plate inside a finished SVG shop at 100% before generating the rest; fall back to flat SVG silhouettes.
Typed 'NAIRA GALLI' on the plate of every cover needs the owner's yes (it is the brand name in Velista, not the wordmark).
graftable: Loop rule: frame 0 = end card = the closed state, and every ambient period divides the loop length (Galli's discipline is the tightest written).
The shutter-down end card for any shop-front bay (NIWAS P1/P2 could end on their own painted shutter).
P4's stroke-written money-order form + stamp as a Bhaubeej mechanic.
P7's eye chart that spells the series name, then the last line becomes the stones: a reusable proof device.
Row strips drawn as one 3,240 px image so gutters never break the street.

scores.criteria: 1 motion-native 9: the drawer sliding out at the site's own 1.1 s IS the curtain; flats hinge up like a pop-up book; the piece rises through a trap like the website's solitaire; nothing fades except light (the box's own clip-never-fade rule). The closest tie to motion the owner has already tuned herself. 2 calm 7: the constants are hers (1.1/1.0 s drawer, 3.2 s float, glint every 4 s, push-in <= 3%), but P8's Tree 3 trembles at 1.6 Hz and the crepe sun wobbles +-3 deg (deliberate jitter), P10's drops swing on 0.5 s counts under a 0.25 s LED checker chase, and P6's bulb 9 flickers. 3 storyboard 7: precise and often very funny (P4's typed line struck out mid-word, P6's bulb 9, P2's moon stopping halfway), but every one of seven reels spends ~8 s on the same wrapper (bells, pull, rise, close, programme, return), the first 1.5 s is a still box while the bells ring, and the stage itself is a ~212-240 px band in a 1920 frame with only a 3% push-in, so the show plays small on a phone. 4 loop 9: last frame pixel-identical to first via THE RETURN; carousel loops start on the cover. 5 end card 7: the programme over the shut box with the ticket is consistent and on-brand, but holds are short (P6 0.9 s, others 1.5-2.0 s). 6 sound 9: three soft bells open every reel (the Marathi third bell): recognisable with the screen off; one instrument family per show; paper, drawer and glass foley timed. 7 grid 6: eleven identical boxes on one shelf line is a system, but at 391x521 the jewellery is tiny (P3 tower pieces ~45-75 px, most stages a sliver under a dominant lid), so the grid sells the packaging more than the pieces; sameness risk the proposal itself admits. 8 feasibility 7: demo-box.html already proves the CSS 3D drawer and pop-up layers, and a cover prototype exists; pieces stay small so no upsampling; but flats inside one preserve-3d context risk face-sorting errors (2D fallback written), and 16 AI plates include gouache scrolls, a crayon forest and paper-craft chairs, elephants and karwa. 9 finish 6: the one V3 render that exists (work/v3box/proto/p2-full.png) is flat and clip-art: a gradient box, a karwa built of circles, a dark stage floor dominating the drawer; a 10/10 finish needs the real box's pearlescent card, soft shadows and a believable bracelet round a pot's neck, none of which the CSS route gives for free. 10 plan 8: one stage kit built once (box, flat, trap, rod card, fly, light, glint, ticket, programme), realistic effort estimate, 2D compositing fallback. AMATEUR RISK BY POST: P1 med (CSS box finish, AI curtain) · P2 high (karwa + bracelet masked round its neck; prototype already reads clip-art) · P3 med-high (four stacked CSS boxes, tiny pieces) · P4 low-med (page, typing, paper heart) · P5 med (locker wall; worn Higgsfield plate check) · P6 low-med (SVG ladi) · P7 high (three AI gouache panels on a scroll, paper bust, blouse swaps) · P8 high (crayon AI backdrop, crepe trees, tremble) · P9 high (AI paper-craft chairs, loupe) · P10 med (tape and LED floor drawn in stage perspective) · P11 med-high (AI laser-cut arch and elephants) · P12 med. No real footage or character animation; moderate CSS 3D.
best_posts: P4 HE WILL NEVER SAY THE LINE.: the script types itself, 'Didi, I love y' is struck through mid-word, a paper heart pops up and the Heartbead rises into it: the tightest native gag of the run and cheap to build.
P6 ONE BULB IS ALWAYS OUT.: the ladi flies in, switches on, chases, bulb 9 flickers hopefully and dies, the Fine Tennis glint never goes out.
P2 EVEN THE KARWA DRESSED UP.: the moon on its rod stops halfway (late, as every year) then rises: good timing, if the karwa can be made to look real.
P1 PLEASE TAKE YOUR SEATS.: the whole ritual once, three coloured pools meeting on the Prism Riviere.
weakest_posts: P8 YOU WERE TREE 3.: a 1.6 Hz tremble and a wobbling sun are the jitter the owner rejects; crayon AI backdrop and crepe trees are the most likely to read amateur.
P3 FOUR BOXES.: four stacked boxes with pieces at ~45-75 px in the grid: the tile shows packaging, not jewellery.
P9 THE FRONT ROW SEES IT ALL.: AI paper-craft chairs from behind, two single huggies on a riser, a loupe: busy for a small stage.
P10 REHEARSALS: THREE WEEKS.: swinging on 0.5 s counts under a 0.25 s LED chase is the fastest motion in the season.
must_fix: Hold every programme >= 2.5 s (P6 0.9 s; others 1.5-2.0 s).
Cut the shared wrapper after Show 01 to <= 4 s (bells over the pull, one hinge, no full return) so each reel's scene gets the time.
Let the camera lean in from the stalls during the scene (to ~1.4-1.6x on the stage, within cut-out resolution) or crop covers to a stage view; the 3% push-in keeps the show a sliver on a phone.
P8: replace the tremble with one slow lean and recovery (>= 1.2 s); still the sun. P10: LED chase to >= 0.6 s steps, swings to 1.0 s half-periods.

Raise the box's finish before building shows: AP-02 card texture, soft contact shadow, rim light, a paper floor that is not near-black; or render the box states from the site's three.js scene and composite flats in 2D (the written fallback).
Enlarge pieces on covers so each reads >= 120 px in the grid; reconsider P3's tower for the cover.
graftable: Three soft bells as a sonic signature for any series.
Reuse of the owner's own REVEAL constants (drawer 1.1 s out / 1.0 s home, glint every 4 s, float 3.2 s, clip never fade) as the house tempo.
P4's typed-and-struck line + pop-up heart as a Bhai Dooj mechanic.
P6's 'bulb 9 is out' as the joke for any string-light scene (NIWAS's terrace).
Children's Day as 'you were Tree 3' (told without the tremble).

beats_A_and_B: A (Matching Centre) is a stills feed with two reels, one of which the craft judge called the least conceptual reel of the four; B (MANGAL) has three reels and carries the density and drawing risk of a dozen bespoke domestic objects. On motion every V3 beats both, because all twelve posts move. On the full 10/10 bar: NAIRA NIWAS beats both clearly: motion is the idea at post and season level, the grid becomes one lit building (a composition neither A nor B attempts), its pace matches the owner's numbers, its interiors are photographs (lower amateur risk than B's drawn objects), and its finale avoids the ruby both A and B close on. DRAWN FROM LIFE beats both conceptually (the only option whose thesis is carried by the motion itself) but only if a P1 proof shows the AI line plates drawing on like a pen; if that fails it falls below A, whose real photography on swatches cannot read AI-made. NAIRA GALLI beats both on motion and on a continuous-street grid, but it sits next to A's and B's own territory (a shop, a vernacular world, the bangle-soap and honest-Dhanteras moves) and today its price cards are unreadable; it wins only after its holds and P1 pull-back are fixed. THE BOX THEATRE beats both on motion-nativeness and owner affinity (her box, her tempo, a bell signature), but its tiles sell the packaging more than the piece, and its only render is below A's finish; it ties rather than beats them until the box looks like the real card box and the stage is shown closer.
recommendation: Build NAIRA NIWAS (v3-proposal-free.json) as Variation 3. It is the only plan where the movement, the grid and the season are one idea, it runs at the owner's own tempo, and its build is one 2D world plus photographs. Graft: (1) DRAWN FROM LIFE's match-dissolve as each window's piece entrance (a drawn outline traced from the cut-out alpha, retracting as the photograph develops) and its process-flipbook logic for the carousels whose slide 1 is only a sweep (P2, P5, P11); (2) GALLI's loop discipline (ambient periods divide the loop; frame 0 = cover/closed state) and a painted shutter end card for the two shop bays; (3) BOX THEATRE's sound signature, as one building sound (a society doorbell or the lift bell) on every establishing shot, and its bulb-9 joke on the terrace lights. Before committing, spend one day on a proof: C-WORLD at 1/3 scale with all twelve closed bays, the kandil's 10 s turn, and P1 rendered end to end and pulled frame by frame at 0.0, 0.8, 2.6, 5.4, 6.9, 10.0 and 12.6 s; then the 12-cover composite over LAC / flower / BONE at 391x521. Apply NIWAS's must-fixes (end-card holds >= 2.5 s, flutter loops slowed, the terrace blush kept off tan, one box render path, WhatsApp promise signed off or cut). Runner-up if the owner wants a softer, editorial V3: DRAWN FROM LIFE, gated on its P1 proof.
